variables.name: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH

readers.mechanism: systemd ${NAME} expansion in ExecStop= (fusermount3 -u). The command runs at each stop of the service.
systemd ${NAME} expansion in ExecStopPost= (rmdir). The command runs after each stop of the service.

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_host, rinzler_mock, runtron (outside this area)
packaging/systemd/rinzler-descriptor (outside this area; the unit runs it at line 48)
readers.mechanism: shell $NAME expansion of a variable that the script does not assign

setters.value: /var/run/rinzler/%i (systemd replaces %i with the instance name, the text after the @ in the unit name)
setters.why: gives each rinzler instance its own FUSE stats mount directory

variables.values: Path to a directory. The unit passes the text unchanged to fusermount3, install and rmdir. The helper script rinzler-descriptor accepts only an absolute path with at least two components. It prints an error and exits with status 1 for an empty value, a relative path, the path /, and a one-component path such as /foo.
variables.default: Under the packaged unit the value is /var/run/rinzler/<instance> (line 7). Without the unit, when the variable is unset or empty, rinzler and runtron use <repository root>/stats when the executable path contains /gen/ and a repository root is found. Otherwise they use /opt/positron/stats.
variables.effect: Selects the directory where rinzler mounts its FUSE stats tree (statistics shown as files). Before each start, the unit unmounts any old mount at that path and creates the directory with owner positron and mode 0750. At each stop, the unit unmounts the path and removes the directory.
variables.notes: The unit comment (lines 20-25) says /etc/rinzler/instance-<instance>.env, written by platformd, may override the value. README.stats.md:46 says platformd writes RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH=/var/run/rinzler/<N> into that file. /opt/positron/user/config.env is loaded too (line 43). The checkout does not say which of the two files wins when both set the name. rinzler-descriptor runs with set -eu (line 7), so an unset variable stops the script with an error. Inside the binary the --fuse-mount flag wins over the variable (src/rinzler.cpp:4724, src/runtron.cpp:490). When --instance idx,N has N greater than 1, the binary appends /instance-<idx> unless RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED is exactly 1. The repository root of the fallback is REPO_ROOT_OVERRIDE when that variable is set and not empty (h/common/paths.hpp:67). rinzler_proxy is built with RINZLER_NO_FUSE_MOUNT and never mounts, so it ignores this variable (src/rinzler.cpp:129-135, src/CMakeLists.txt:194). packaging/tron-host/README:81-82 says a rinzler_host that a person starts by hand makes its mount in the working directory. The code gives /opt/positron/stats for that case (src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:36), so the README sentence holds only when the working directory is /opt/positron. The last two reader sites are outside this area. Other areas hold more readers and setters (CI workflows, bin/slice, bin/fuse_cleanup.py, bin/ci/benchmark_lib.py, tests).

variables.name: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_host, rinzler_mock, runtron (outside this area)

setters.why: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH in the unit is already per instance, so the binary must not append /instance-<idx>

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 turns the per-instance suffix off. Any other text, including true, yes, 0 and an empty value, leaves the suffix on.
variables.default: Unset: when --instance idx,N has N greater than 1 and idx is 0 or more, the binary appends /instance-<idx> to the resolved FUSE mount path.
variables.effect: With the value 1, rinzler uses the mount path from RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH or from the built-in fallback without the /instance-<idx> suffix. Under the packaged unit this keeps the mount at /var/run/rinzler/<instance>.
variables.notes: The unit comment (lines 8-14) says that removing the line gives no startup error. The mount then moves to a path such as /var/run/rinzler/0/instance-0, and the tronstats scanner of platformd no longer finds it. The unit comment (lines 20-25) says the instance environment file must not set this name, because a value from EnvironmentFile= replaces the Environment= value. A path given with --fuse-mount is used unchanged in every case. No file of this area reads the name. The reader site is outside this area.

variables.name: RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock (all built from src/rinzler.cpp; outside this area)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv; the result is parsed by parse_save_tokens_enabled (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:290)

setters.why: states the default (save_tokens enabled) in the packaged unit, so that an operator can see the switch and override it to 0

variables.values: Exactly the text 0 or the text 1. Any other text, including an empty value, makes rinzler log 'RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS validation failed' and exit with status 1 at startup.
variables.default: Unset means enabled, the same as 1.
variables.effect: With 1, the server accepts the save_tokens request parameter (a development-only parameter that captures the token ids of a request). With 0, a chat or completions request that asks for save_tokens gets HTTP 400 with the message 'save_tokens' is disabled on this server.
variables.notes: The unit sets 1 with Environment=. By the unit comment (lines 22-24), a value in /etc/rinzler/instance-<instance>.env or in /opt/positron/user/config.env replaces it. README.proxy.md:152-153 names /opt/positron/user/config.env as the place to set 0, followed by a restart of the unit. RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1 together with RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0 fails startup (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:314-316). No file of this area reads the name. The reader site is outside this area.

variables.name: CPUAFFINITY

readers.mechanism: systemd ${NAME} expansion in ExecStart= (argument of taskset -c)
systemd ${NAME} expansion in ExecStart= (argument of taskset -c)

variables.values: A CPU list in the form that the -c option of /usr/bin/taskset accepts. The unit passes the text to taskset. TRON code does not parse it.
variables.default: No default. The unit and the drop-in give no fallback, and no file in the checkout sets the name. The value must come from /etc/rinzler/instance-<instance>.env or from /opt/positron/user/config.env.
variables.effect: Sets the CPUs that the rinzler process may run on. The unit starts the program through taskset -c with this list. With the tron-host drop-in the program is rinzler_host.
variables.notes: The name appears only in these two files of the checkout. Not determined from the checkout: what systemd and taskset do when the variable is unset or empty, and how systemd splits the braces form into arguments. systemd and taskset are not in the checkout. The unit sets SyslogIdentifier=rinzler (line 64) so that the journal does not show taskset as the program name (comment at line 63). The unit comment at line 20 says platformd writes the instance environment file. The checkout does not show which names platformd writes there, except RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH (README.stats.md:46). Confidence is medium because the unset behaviour and the writer of the value are outside the checkout.

variables.name: RZ_CLI_ARGS
variables.values: Command-line arguments for rinzler. The unit puts them after the program name. The checkout does not list which flags the writer of the value puts there.
variables.default: No default. The unit and the drop-in give no fallback, and no file in the checkout sets the name. The value must come from /etc/rinzler/instance-<instance>.env or from /opt/positron/user/config.env.
variables.effect: Supplies the command line of the rinzler service instance. With the tron-host drop-in, the program is rinzler_host and the drop-in adds --host 127.0.0.1 after these arguments.
variables.notes: The name appears only in these two files of the checkout. packaging/tron-host/README:72 and :121-122 say platformd passes --model-path, --app-cores, --dev-cores and --numa to rinzler_host. The README does not name this variable, but the unit has no other place for arguments. The form without braces is used. Not determined from the checkout: how systemd splits the value into arguments and what it does when the variable is unset. Confidence is medium for that reason.

variables.name: TRON_LOG_DIR

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, runtron, and programs that call pos_startup_host of libpos (function init_logging; outside this area)

setters.why: rinzler writes alderaan.log into its working directory by default, and the positron user cannot write to /opt/positron (file comment, lines 8-10)

variables.values: Path to a directory. The program writes the log file <directory>/alderaan.log there.
variables.default: Unset: the log file is alderaan.log in the current working directory, or alderaan-root.log when the effective user is root. An empty value gives the relative name alderaan.log for every user.
variables.effect: Moves the rotating log file alderaan.log to the given directory. The code gives the spdlog rotating file sink a size limit of 512 MiB per file and a file count of 3. The same messages still go to stderr.
variables.notes: The drop-in also sets LogsDirectory=rinzler/%i (line 17). The drop-in is for test and development hosts only (file comment, line 1). The packaged rinzler@.service does not set this variable, and its working directory is /opt/positron (packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:6). init_logging sets up the log only on its first call in a process. If the logger cannot be created, the program prints 'Log initialization failed' and exits with status 1 (src/system/spdlog.cpp:64-67). No file of this area reads the name. The reader site is outside this area. bin/slice also sets the variable (other area).

variables.name: RZ_KV_CACHE_GB

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock (main in src/rinzler.cpp; outside this area)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv; the text is parsed with std::stoull at line 4578

setters.why: limits the persistent KV cache to 1 GB on small test hosts; the file comment (line 13) says to scale it to the RAM of the host

variables.values: Unsigned integer, in GB. The code shifts the number left by 30 bits to get bytes (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:458). The text is parsed with std::stoull. An empty or non-numeric value makes std::stoull throw. No try block surrounds the call in main, so the program terminates.
variables.default: Unset: the target is half of the hugepage count, n_hugepages / 2 (src/system/system.cpp:2539-2541). The default hugepage count is 16 (h/system/config.hpp:12), so the default target is 8 GB.
variables.effect: Sets the target size of the persistent KV cache (stored attention keys and values of earlier tokens), for all models together. The program logs 'RZ_KV_CACHE_GB set to <value>'.
variables.notes: The system flag --kv-cache-gb writes the same setting later in startup and so replaces the value (src/system/system.cpp:2047, reached from src/rinzler.cpp:4906). When the arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) is active, the program ignores this variable and logs one warning that names it (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:86). The drop-in is for test and development hosts only. The packaged rinzler@.service does not set this variable. No file of this area reads the name. The reader site is outside this area.

variables.name: CI
variables.values: Any non-empty value counts as set. The text is not parsed.
variables.default: Unset or empty: a hook command whose tool is missing prints 'Skipping: <tool> not found' and succeeds.
variables.effect: When set, a missing lint tool is an error. The hook command prints 'ERROR: <tool> not found' and exits with status 1. This applies to clang-format, ruff, nixfmt, shfmt, fourmolu, uv and the lint-notes checker. For rustfmt, a missing cargo is an error when CI or IN_NIX_SHELL is set.
variables.notes: 9 reader sites in lefthook.yml: lines 57, 110, 149, 163, 190, 221, 237, 275 and 302. The last three are the commands fourmolu, lock-freshness (uv) and lint-notes. The ruff commands do not look at CI when TRON_NIX_LINT_SHELL is 1 or when ci/.venv/bin/ruff is executable. No file in this area sets CI. Other areas also read CI.

variables.name: TRON_NIX_LINT_SHELL

setters.why: the lefthook wrapper script of the Nix shells exports it before it starts lefthook (outside this area)
attribute of the Nix lint development shell (outside this area)
attribute of the Nix lint-toolchain check derivation (outside this area)

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 enables it. Anything else is off.
variables.default: Unset: ruff-format and ruff-check use ci/.venv/bin/ruff when that file is executable, else ruff from PATH. agent-guidance uses ci/.venv/bin/python when that file is executable, else python3 from PATH. A missing nixfmt is skipped unless CI is set.
variables.effect: With 1, the hook commands use the tools that the Nix lint shell puts on PATH. ruff-format and ruff-check run ruff from PATH, and agent-guidance runs python3 from PATH, without looking at ci/.venv. A missing nixfmt becomes an error.
variables.notes: The setter sites are in flake.nix, outside this area. bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh:67, which the ci-pins hook command runs (lefthook.yml:250), reads the same variable (other area).

variables.name: IN_NIX_SHELL

setters.why: the lefthook wrapper script of the Nix shells exports it before it starts lefthook (outside this area)
attribute of the Nix lint-toolchain check derivation (outside this area)

variables.values: Any non-empty value counts as set. The text is not parsed.
variables.default: Unset or empty, with CI also unset or empty: when the check 'rust/run-cargo --tron-check-cargo-available' exits with status 69 (cargo unavailable), the rustfmt hook prints 'Skipping: cargo not found' and succeeds.
variables.effect: When set, the rustfmt hook does not skip a missing cargo. It prints 'ERROR: Rust Cargo availability check failed' and exits with the status of the check.
variables.notes: Nix itself also sets this variable inside its shells. That fact is not in the checkout. The setter sites are in flake.nix, outside this area. flake.nix sets the name at six lines in total. The four lines not listed above (1172, 2123, 2173, 2237) set the value pure for other derivations. This pass did not trace whether lefthook runs inside them. GNUmakefile and other files read the same variable (other areas).

variables.name: GHCRTS

readers.program: ingest (Haskell model compiler, executable ingest in ingest/tron-ingest.cabal)
readers.mechanism: read by the GHC runtime system, not by TRON source. The executable is linked with -rtsopts (line 166). Line 173 is the cabal comment that names the variable.
read by the GHC runtime system, not by TRON source. The test program is linked with -rtsopts (line 204). Line 196 is the cabal comment that names the variable.

variables.values: GHC runtime options, for example -N128 (the number of runtime threads). The GHC runtime parses the text. TRON code does not.
variables.default: Unset: only the options built into the program apply. They are -N32 -A32m -H128m for ingest (line 174) and -N32 -A32m -H128m -ki64k for ingest-tests (line 205).
variables.effect: Changes runtime options of the ingest program and of its test suite at run time. The cabal comments give the examples 'GHCRTS=-N128 make build' and 'GHCRTS=-N128 cabal test'.
variables.notes: The cabal comments (lines 167-173 and 190-196) say GHC 9.12 supports at most 256 capabilities, so a bare -N fails on a host with more than 256 logical CPUs. The built-in value is therefore a fixed -N32. The checkout says only that GHCRTS overrides the built-in options. How the runtime combines the two is GHC behaviour and is not in the checkout. .github/workflows/ingest-coverage.yml:126 mentions the variable in an error message (other area). No file in the checkout sets GHCRTS. Confidence is medium because no TRON source line performs the read.

dynamic_sites.description: EnvironmentFile=/etc/rinzler/instance-%i.env. systemd loads every NAME=value line of this file into the environment of the rinzler instance, so the names are not fixed in the unit. This is the per-instance file. The unit comment (lines 20-25) says platformd writes it, that it may override RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH, and that it must not set RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED. README.stats.md:46 says platformd writes RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH there. The unit takes CPUAFFINITY and RZ_CLI_ARGS from the service environment and sets neither, so they must come from this file or from the file at line 43. The path has no '-' prefix, unlike line 43. Any variable that rinzler reads can be set here.

EnvironmentFile=-/opt/positron/user/config.env. Optional file: the comment at line 42 says the unit tolerates its absence. It is the file a person edits to set variables for every rinzler instance on the host (README.proxy.md:182-183). systemd loads every NAME=value line into the environment of each instance. Any variable that rinzler reads can be set here, for example RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0 (README.proxy.md:152-153).

bin/yq (prebuilt third-party binary in this area) reads the variables that a query names with strenv(NAME) or env(NAME). The names come from the query text of the caller, not from the binary. The only such caller in the checkout is this line, with SERVER_TYPE and RESOURCE_KEY. Line 21 of the same script sets both for that one command. The entries for the two names belong to area shell-ci.

notes:
Coverage: 272 files listed. 270 are text and were all searched with several patterns (getenv, lookupEnv, getEnv, getEnvironment, setEnv, System.Environment, System.Posix, System.Process, environ, export, $NAME, ${NAME}, $(NAME), $ENV{NAME}, Environment=, EnvironmentFile=, upper-case identifiers). Every hit was read in context. 2 files are prebuilt binaries (see files_skipped). Result of this verification: no name is missing from the first inventory. All 12 entries are in scope. 7 entries have corrected or completed facts (see changes). The other 5 entries were checked against the code and stand as they were. 

Where a person sets variables for the rinzler service: (1) /opt/positron/user/config.env, optional, applies to every instance (rinzler@.service line 43). (2) /etc/rinzler/instance-<instance>.env, one per instance, written by platformd (line 26). (3) The unit itself, installed as /etc/systemd/system/rinzler@.service (CMakeLists.txt:780), has three Environment= lines: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH=/var/run/rinzler/%i (line 7), RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED=1 (line 15), RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=1 (line 19). (4) The tron-host drop-in, copied by hand to /etc/systemd/system/rinzler@.service.d/90-rinzler-host.conf on test and development hosts only (packaging/tron-host/README:125-131), has two Environment= lines: TRON_LOG_DIR=/var/log/rinzler/%i (line 18) and RZ_KV_CACHE_GB=1 (line 19). The unit comment (lines 22-24) says a key from an EnvironmentFile= replaces the same key from Environment=. The checkout does not say which EnvironmentFile= wins when both files set one name. packaging/postinst:41-43 runs systemctl daemon-reload after a package upgrade and does not restart running instances (other area). 

packaging/positron-dice/dice.service and dice-payloads.slice have no Environment= line, no EnvironmentFile= line and no $NAME expansion. The unit starts '/opt/positron/bin/dice daemon run' (line 12) only when /etc/positron/dice.yaml has mode: shared (ExecCondition at line 11). The unit names no file in which a person sets variables for the Dice daemon. 

Role and reader sites: for the four set_only names (RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED, RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS, TRON_LOG_DIR, RZ_KV_CACHE_GB) no file of this area reads the name. The reader sites listed for them are C++ files of other areas. They were read to fill values, default and effect. 

Haskell ingest sources (127 .hs files, plus the cabal script bin/lint-notes): no call of getEnv, lookupEnv, getEnvironment or setEnv, and no import of System.Environment except getArgs in bin/lint-notes:65. No System.Process use. The words env and environment in these files mean the binding environment of the model representation, not the process environment. The generators emit C++ (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs, ingest/src/Cpp.hs) and Python (ingest/src/BulkPython.hs, ingest/src/TypedFxPython.hs). The emitted text contains no getenv, os.environ or os.getenv. The emitted Python uses argparse only, with fixed defaults (ingest/src/BulkPython.hs:983-988, ingest/src/TypedFxPython.hs:713-718). The emitted C++ calls runtime functions of the TRON headers, for example outer_state.recommend_n_main_helpers() (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:1465). Environment reads behind such runtime functions belong to the C++ areas (for example TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS and TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS in h/tron/models/model.hpp:74 and :81). ingest/tron-ingest.cabal:158 lists Paths_tron_ingest, a module that Cabal generates. No .hs file imports it, so no TRON code calls it. The test suite runs under the sydtest library. Variables that sydtest itself may read are not named in the checkout and are not listed. The GHC runtime of the ingest programs reads GHCRTS (entry above). ingest/build-all.sh:111 exports HPCTIXFILE for coverage runs of the ingest program (other area). No file of this area names HPCTIXFILE. 

Names that appear in this area only as documentation or comments, and are read elsewhere (not listed as entries): TRON_TP_BIN (usage comment in bin/expert_distribution.sql:8; bin/analyze_kv_duration:30 reads it), TSAN_OPTIONS (usage comment in t/tsan/suppressions.txt:6; GNUmakefile:717-724 sets it), TRON_HOST_MIN_TRON (packaging/tron-host/README:151; GNUmakefile:627 reads it), TRON_FEATURE_BRANCH_BUILD (packaging/tron-host/README:204; bin/get-version.sh:17 reads it), and the make variables DEBUG, STATIC, CROSS_COMPILE, RHOST, RUSER of the vendored iotools (bin/iotools-1.5/README; bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile uses them). No comment in this area names a variable that nothing reads. 

Text that looks like a variable but is not one: %i in the units is a systemd specifier (the instance name). $ORIGIN in packaging/tron-host/README is a dynamic-linker token. "$prev:0" in t/proxy/prompts/*.json is a replay placeholder. $run-tron-tests and similar words in .agents/skills/*/agents/openai.yaml are skill names. BUILD_*_MODELS and DEV_MODEL_CONFIG in config/*.yaml comments are CMake options. TRON_FUSE_STATS_ENABLED in src/system/fuse_stats_config.hpp.in is a CMake definition. 

.ccache/ccache.conf is the file that CCACHE_CONFIGPATH points to (GNUmakefile:101, CMakePresets.json:14, other areas). The file itself reads no variable. No wrapper function is defined or called in this area. The TOML, JSON, YAML, cfg and other data files of the area contain no environment name beyond those listed above.
